ESEN

Anthropologist · researcher · educator

I investigate how we construct partial ways of knowing and acting upon the world.

My work brings together ethnography, pedagogy and material experimentation to examine how experiences, organisms and environments are translated into categories, data, instruments and modes of action. I am currently conducting doctoral ethnographic research in plant biotechnology laboratories in Chile.

An operation

Ongoing research · PhD

Haciendo coherente la vida

An ethnography of plant biotechnology laboratories in Chile.

Biotechnology does not work with forms of life that are entirely stable or controllable. Producing knowledge and intervening in living organisms requires materials, techniques, biological rhythms, experiments, institutions and expectations of the future to be brought temporarily into coordination. My research examines how these coordinations are constructed and sustained, and what happens when they are interrupted or overflow their intended bounds.

Designing conditions forlearning by doing and thinking with others

My teaching practice has developed through the creation of materials, learning sequences and forms of guidance. I approach teaching as a practice of mediation that allows people to engage gradually with complex problems, try out ways of addressing them and review what they produce with others.

The cases gathered here show three scales of this work: turning several years of teaching into a reusable guide, supporting students as they formulate their research projects and organising an applied learning experience in collaboration with an organisation.

Three disciplines, one trajectory shaped through sedimentation

My trajectory brings together psychology, sociology and anthropology as part of a deliberate effort to broaden the scales through which I understand knowledge and action. From the outset, I wanted to move towards sociology and anthropology because I found overly individualising explanations insufficient. Sociology allowed me to study policies, institutions and technologies of government; anthropology later offered a way to engage with the concrete practices that the institutional analysis in my master’s thesis could not reach. This direction was present from an early stage, although I did not always know precisely how the disciplines would come together.

Something similar occurred with my training in computing and data: I sensed that they could contribute to my work, but their place became clearer through specific projects and problems. At each stage, the objects, scales and research methods changed. What persisted was an interest in the processes through which situated experiences and relationships take on forms that allow them to be interpreted, organised and acted upon, while also making them measurable, standardised, able to circulate and governable.

Psychology2018

Psychologist and BA in PsychologyUniversidad de La Serena

ThesisEthos moral de la formación profesional docente: significados posibles en estudiantes de primer año de pedagogía de la Universidad de La Serena.

My initial training focused on educational processes and on how people interpret their own experience. I took part in research on subjective theories, teachers’ perceptions of time and teacher education, and examined the moral meanings at play in initial teacher education.

I later worked as a school coexistence officer in a rural school and then as municipal school coexistence coordinator at the Municipality of Punitaqui. This brought those questions into contact with rural schools, public regulations, administrative records and intersectoral coordination.

That experience was one of the reasons I moved into other disciplines. I came to understand that intersectoral work required familiarity with how other organisations operated and with the languages they used. When I began to recognise, in the words of other participants, concepts that I had tried to bring into circulation, I saw a concrete sign that we were beginning to understand one another.

Sociology2023

MA in SociologyUniversidad Alberto Hurtado

ThesisSurgimiento y evolución de la convivencia escolar en Chile a través de la política nacional (2002–2019): la creación de un dominio de intervención y el ensamblaje de una herramienta de gobierno.

My decision to pursue a master’s degree grew out of my daily engagement with regulatory documents while working as a municipal coordinator. That experience shifted my attention from individual interpretations towards public policies, organisations and technologies of government.

I examined how situated relational conflicts were transformed into standardised categories, protocols and indicators that could circulate and guide interventions at a distance. The historical reconstruction showed that these forms of intervention did not emerge all at once, but gradually took shape through earlier developments, disputes, reformulations and institutional projections.

During this period, I began working more directly in academia, combining research and teaching across Psychology, Sociology and Special Education. Between 2023 and August 2026, I helped establish and manage the Centro de Intervención e Investigación en Psicología Educacional (CIPSE-UCEN), where I coordinated research, public and community engagement, and the production of teaching materials. Between 2025 and August 2026, I also supervised the formulation, implementation and writing of undergraduate research projects and theses in Psychology.

Anthropology2025–present

PhD in Anthropology, in progressPontificia Universidad Católica de ChileCandidacy approved in July 2026

Doctoral thesisHaciendo coherente la vida: una etnografía en laboratorios de biotecnología vegetal en Chile.

I am currently conducting ethnographic research into knowledge production in plant biotechnology. The research follows relationships among plants, techniques, instruments, data, public institutions and companies, attending to the different temporalities that converge in scientific work. The question is no longer only how a social experience becomes governable.

It also asks how materially heterogeneous forms of life acquire coherence as scientific objects, information and promises of intervention. The research shifts these concerns towards operations at the molecular scale and the processes through which biological matter is transformed into comparable information that can circulate.

Additional training

I have pursued additional training in data, IT infrastructure, design, teaching and public management. These areas of study broaden the resources I draw on to conduct research, teach and build. Their practical application can be seen throughout the projects section.

Data and IT infrastructure

Data analysis and curation, databases, object-oriented programming, data networks and server administration.

Design and mediation

Customer experience, data and innovation, curating, consumer psychology, art and public space.

Teaching

Higher education teaching, instructional design, self-regulated learning, social-emotional learning and reading promotion.

Management and public sector

Public management, territorial support for educational improvement, institutional use of data, probity and transparency.
